condition_specific: stomach, colon, rectum, skin, prostate, testis, or brain cancer; non-Hodgkin's lymphoma; multiple myeloma; malignant melanoma; renal cell carcinoma
notes: CORRECTED (2026-08-07 research): SB 2551 (2019, Ch. 701) removed the original exposure-based/IARC-referenced eligibility test entirely for this presumption -- the firefighter need only be diagnosed with one of the 11 enumerated cancer types above; no showing of heat/smoke/radiation/carcinogen exposure is required (that requirement predates the 2019 amendment and no longer applies). Rebuttal per § 607.058 requires preponderance of evidence; ALJ must consider whether a qualified expert relying on evidence-based medicine stated the opinion. Tobacco exclusion: disease known to be caused by tobacco use bars the presumption if firefighter/EMT or smoking spouse used tobacco.

condition_specific: acute myocardial infarction, stroke
notes: Requires that while on duty, firefighter was engaged in nonroutine stressful or strenuous physical activity (fire suppression, rescue, hazmat, EMS, emergency response, or nonroutine training exercise) AND the AMI/stroke occurred during that activity. Does not include clerical, administrative, or nonmanual activities. Tobacco exclusion applies.

notes: § 607.054 covers TB (infectious) and other lung/respiratory diseases (respiratory) in one statutory provision; split into two rows per schema rules. condition_specific: PTSD (post-traumatic stress disorder)
notes: Applies to firefighters subject to certification by Texas Commission on Fire Protection whose principal duties are firefighting and aircraft crash and rescue, employed by a political subdivision. PTSD must be diagnosed as caused by an event in course and scope of employment, and preponderance of evidence must show the event was a substantial contributing factor. Mental/emotional injury from legitimate personnel action (transfer, promotion, demotion, termination) is not compensable per § 408.006.

condition_specific: smallpox; disability or death from preventative immunization against smallpox or other disease
notes: Cannot be rebutted by evidence that immunization was not required by employer, not required by law, or received voluntarily. 5-year service and pre-employment exam requirements apply via § 607.052 applicability section. Disease must be discovered during employment per § 607.052(a)(3). Tobacco exclusion applies under § 607.052(b)(4).

condition_specific: Retiree critical-illness/health benefit — triggered by post-retirement diagnosis (within 3 years of retirement) of an enumerated § 607.055 cancer, acute myocardial infarction, or stroke
post_termination_formula: Diagnosis must occur within 3 years (36 months) of retirement
notes: This is not a workers' compensation presumption. It is a freestanding, mandatory employer-funded benefit: either a lump-sum or 3-month critical-illness supplemental income payment (the lesser of the retiree's final annual salary or $100,000, adjusted for inflation every 5 years), or comparable post-retirement health coverage. It is structurally similar to Florida's § 112.1816 program. Effective September 1, 2025, it applies only to firefighters and peace officers retiring on or after January 1, 2026 from a department or agency with 50 or more personnel. Political subdivisions that already provide comparable retiree health coverage are exempt. EMTs are not covered.
